Let <MATH_0001> be a <MATH_0002>-morphism of stacks in groupoids
over <MATH_0003>. Assume <MATH_0004> is representable by algebraic
spaces, flat, surjective, and locally of finite presentation. Then
<MATH_0005>
is surjective on objects.

It suffices to prove the following: For any field <MATH_0001>
and object <MATH_0002> of <MATH_0003> over <MATH_0004> there exists
an integer <MATH_0005> and an object <MATH_0006> of
<MATH_0007> with <MATH_0008>.
Namely, in this case we see that <MATH_0009> is surjective on objects in the
strong sense that an extension of the field is not needed.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Denote <MATH_0010> the algebraic space over <MATH_0011>
representing the <MATH_0012>-fibre product
<MATH_0013>.
By assumption the morphism <MATH_0014> is surjective and
locally of finite presentation (and flat). In particular <MATH_0015> is
nonempty. Choose a nonempty affine scheme <MATH_0016> and an <ACCENT_0001>tale morphism
<MATH_0017>. Note that <MATH_0018> is (flat), surjective,
and locally of finite presentation (by
Morphisms of Spaces,
Definition <REF_0001>).
Pick a closed point <MATH_0019> where <MATH_0020> is Cohen-Macaulay
(i.e., <MATH_0021> is Cohen-Macaulay at <MATH_0022>), see
More on Morphisms,
Lemma <REF_0002>.
Applying
More on Morphisms,
Lemma <REF_0003>
we find a regular immersion <MATH_0023> with <MATH_0024>.
This implies <MATH_0025> is a closed immersion. Moreover, it follows that
<MATH_0026> is finite (for example by
Algebra, Lemma <REF_0004>).
Hence <MATH_0027> is finite locally free of some degree <MATH_0028>.
Now <MATH_0029> is unramified as the composition
of a closed immersion followed by an <ACCENT_0002>tale morphism
(see
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemmas <REF_0005>,
<REF_0006>, and
<REF_0007>).
Finally, <MATH_0030> is a local complete intersection morphism
as a composition of a regular immersion of schemes and an <ACCENT_0003>tale
morphism of algebraic spaces (see
More on Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0008>
and
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemmas <REF_0009> and
<REF_0010> and
More on Morphisms of Spaces,
Lemmas <REF_0011> and
<REF_0012>).
The morphism <MATH_0031> corresponds to an object <MATH_0032> of <MATH_0033>
over <MATH_0034> together with an isomorphism <MATH_0035>.
We obtain an object <MATH_0036> of
<MATH_0037>. By what was said above about
the morphism <MATH_0038> we see that it actually is an object of the
subcategory <MATH_0039> and we win.
